newsitem.title: INDIA: India yr/yr inflation dips to 6.35 pct - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: India yr/yr inflation dips to 6.35 pct - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told parliament on Friday that the year-on-year inflation rate based on the wholesale price index had fallen to 6.35 percent in figures scheduled to be released on Sunday.
"Next Monday, we will report the inflation rate coming down to 6.35 percent," Chidambaram said in his reply to a debate on the Finance Bill.
He was referring to the government's weekly inflation report which is released on Sunday and reported in newspapers on Monday.
Last Sunday, the government reported that the annual inflation rate as measured by the wholesale price index was 6.54 percent in the week ended on April 19.
Chidambaram was responding to opposition members who in the course of the debate on the Finance Bill had raised concerns over possible increases in inflation.
The lower house of parliament was expected to vote on the Finance Bill, which incorporates the tax and tariff proposals in the government's 1997/98 (April-March) budget package, later on Friday.
